speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The exchanges were demutualised and merged into a single non-member run entity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The essential aim was to put the integrated exchange in a stronger position to hold its own internationally and develop new growth opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Through this demutualisation process, members of the two exchanges, SES and SIMEX, received a fixed dollar amount of shares in SGX and the remaining SGX shares were issued to SEL Holdings Pte Ltd (SEL), a special purpose company designated under the EDMA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SEL placed out some of the SGX shares to new investors and retained the rest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This portion of SGX shares that SEL retained, which I shall refer to as the "Original SGX shares", are currently held by SEL for the benefit of the Financial Sector Development Fund (FSDF).

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS set up FSDF in 1999 to support the development of Singapore as a financial centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: FSDF is controlled and administered by MAS, subject to the directions of the Minister-in-charge of MAS.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The dividends and any proceeds in respect of the Original SGX Shares are channelled towards the FSDF to fund financial sector development initiatives in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These include initiatives which develop sector-wide capabilities and infrastructure, promote financial innovation, upgrade skills and expertise, and support financial education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It should be highlighted that under the EDMA, SEL is not able to exercise or control the exercise of the voting rights attached to the SGX shares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This feature remains unchanged in the proposed amendments to the EDMA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is important because it is not intended for MAS, in its capacity as FSDF’s administrator, to impinge on SGX’s capacity to make business decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This safeguard further enables MAS to play the roles as SGX's regulator and FSDF's administrator without conflict of interest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX announced on 5 August 2021 that it would be implementing a scrip dividend scheme (SDS) to offer its shareholders the option to receive all or part of their dividend entitlement in SGX shares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: SGX has explained that this scheme would allow shareholders to re-invest their cash dividends in SGX’s medium-term growth journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Currently, the EDMA allows SEL to receive new SGX shares where there is no election or choice on the part of the shareholders, such as when bonus shares are issued.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, it does not allow SEL the flexibility to elect to receive new SGX shares when these arise from corporate actions taken by SGX, such as scrip dividend schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For instance, SEL could elect to receive scrip dividends in SGX scrip dividend scheme (SDS), which it is unable to under the current EDMA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Bill will also provide that SGX shares acquired through such participation will be treated in the same manner as the Original SGX shares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It only enables SEL to participate in corporate actions taken by SGX under which SEL may elect to receive new SGX shares.

speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The new SGX shares will be treated the same way as the Original SGX shares.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It is logical, as that is the ownership rights of any shareholders of a listed company.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: However, what interest me on this Bill is the structure in which the shares of SGX are being held and how dividends are used to fund FSDF to support various initiatives set out in the MAS Act.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The EDMA came about because of the demutualisation and merger of the Stock Exchange of Singapore, SIMEX and SCCS.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: SEL is a special purpose vehicle designated to hold the SGX shares, specifically for the benefit of FSDF.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And FSDF is set up to support the promotion of Singapore as a financial centre and is controlled and administered by MAS; subject to the directions of the Minister-in-charge of MAS.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Notwithstanding, Sir, I have a couple of questions for the Minister: I can understand the historical context of this arrangement.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But I want to ask the Minister of State if MAS still sees the continued need for SEL to be the largest shareholder of SGX; and as a result, the holdings of SGX shares would constitute a significant part of the investment for FSDF?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Would FSDF be being better served with a more diversified portfolio and its interest to SGX reduced?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State if the FSDF would also encourage donations or contributions from stakeholders such as financial institutions or industry professionals who have benefited from the development of the financial sector.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Indeed, a Business Times' article in September last year noted that in line with global trends, SGX has seen a flurry of privatisation offers in 2021.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This has meant a decrease in the number of companies listed on the exchange, which is a cause for concern.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: To add to the picture, some commentators have opined that there is a likelihood that money will start flowing to listings in emerging markets.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: They predict that emerging markets themselves may even go as far as to require domestic companies to list locally and to encourage foreign companies who are trying to raise capital within their borders to also list within that jurisdiction rather than look to capital markets in the more established markets such as New York, London, Hong Kong and even Singapore.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Yet, it has also not escaped the notice of many that there are growing concerns about whether SGX has become illiquid and uncompetitive, and that companies looking to widen their capital base would do better to look elsewhere.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Indeed, of late, our homegrown success stories such as Grab and Razor have chosen to list oversees.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: All this has implications for SGX and the liquidity of our local capital markets as our success has historically relied on foreign entities being willing to fundraise by using our domestic market as a platform to access capital in the region.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: While it is good that solid investors have indicated their willingness to invest in SGX, we must not be complacent about the competitiveness of our exchange and take this for granted.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Set against this, I have a few clarifications that I wish to seek of the Minister of State.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: If so, where will funds come from in order for SEL to subscribe for any new SGX shares?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Also, what is MAS' updated position relating to allowing shareholders to increase stakes above 5% and also if an offer is made by another stock exchange to acquire or merge with SGX?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: While, historically, regulators have been somewhat cautious to allow super stock exchange mergers, as evidenced by, for example, the rejection of SGX's bid to acquire the Australian Stock Exchange over a decade ago, recent research into super stock exchanges appears to suggest that there need not be huge concerns about the exploitation of market power of these large exchanges.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Admittedly, though, there may still be concerns of national interests when considering such merger and acquisition (M&A) activity relating to SGX itself.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Next, turning to the beneficiary of the SGX shares held by SEL.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: FSDF's objectives primarily relate to the promotion of Singapore as a financial centre and the development of our financial services industry.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Would the Minister of State be able to give an update if there is any intention to expand the role or impact of the fund, given the potential increase in SGX shares held to its benefit?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Moving on to governance, by which I mean the governance of the board and also the dual role of MAS as both regulator and promoter.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What are the criteria applied to determining whether a director is sufficiently independent for sitting on the board of SEL?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Could the Minister of State consider outlining a clear framework the various factors to be considered when appointing independent directors for SEL for the purposes of greater transparency and confidence?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: As MAS has to both promote and grow the finance industry and also serve as regulator of the industry – in our case, of SGX and our capital markets – what are the processes and frameworks that are put in place to address any conflicts or perceived conflicts that may arise from this?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: For example, in the UK, the Financial Conduct Authority was formed by the carving out of the former Financial Services Authority (FSA) in the wake of the Global Financial Crisis to be able to better focus as it serves its function as the regulator of the finance industry.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I would also like to seek greater clarity from the Minister of State about if and how the amendments to the Act will make it easier for the exchange to compete and stay relevant in the changing landscape, that it will not become moribund one day.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: How would these ensure that our stock market and, by extension, our capital markets and finance industry remain competitive and attractive to investors who are increasingly looking for the next best thing to put their money in?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What steps are our regulators and authorities taking to ensure the sustainability – and, thus, the likelihoods of many of our people employed in these industries – of our capital markets so that they remain healthy when we look to the long term?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.20 pm so that we have more time to do research and figure out how the reserves are being used.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.50 pm until 4.20 pm.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Original SGX shares are also held for the benefit of the Financial Sector Development Fund (FSDF), which is an important vehicle in helping to promote Singapore as a financial hub.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This fund has been assisting companies to upgrade and train their staff to meet the demanding skills in the financial services sector.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: More than that, this fund has also been deployed over the years to carry out research and development projects relating to this sector and develop infrastructure support.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share with the House how well-received is its various grant schemes granted under FSDF this year, especially the Cybersecurity Capability Grant (CCG)?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And are there also any institutions looking into blockchain technology and carbon credit exchanges which have tapped into any of the grants?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And what are the measures to ensure our grant expenditures are aligned with FSDF’s objectives?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The support package comprised new schemes to support digitalisation in smaller financial institutions and fintech firms.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It also supported existing training and talent development programmes to support financial institutions, fintech firms and individuals within the financial services sector in navigating the economic downturn.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is so that Singapore could emerge stronger as a global financial centre in Asia.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With the emergence of the Omicron variant and for future crises, I suppose FSDF would stand ready to support the financial sector if the need arises?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And with the dent caused by the pandemic on our economy, has the FSDF expenditure changed?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How many people took up FSDF’s training support schemes – financial training schemes and IBF training schemes as well as scholarships?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Have there been changes in trends since the EDMA was introduced in 1999?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And the new SGX shares are to be treated the same way as the Original SGX Shares.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: SEL would, with the Minister’s approval, also have the option, like any other shareholders, to receive the dividends in scrip or in cash.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What is the worst-case scenario if this Bill goes through?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In what instances will the Minister not approve the SEL request and will there be an issue of liquidity for FSDF in the worst-case scenario, preferring cash to non-cash equivalents?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My other question relates to sources of funding for FSDF.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The role in which FSDF plays in terms of grants and also talent capability building, as well as the sector’s leadership talent pipeline, will be pivotal for the financial sector's growth and development.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can I ask what other sources of funds feed into FSDF, beyond the SGX cash and scrip dividends and rights issues and others?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: And what is the breakdown of these other sources?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: If the other source is from investment income from the existing assets under management, how volatile is it?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Are there future plans to further diversify the sources of funding for the FSDF?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: SGX – and, for that matter, most countries’ capital market exchanges – continues to be a pivotal player in Singapore’s financial sector growth and development.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is important to ensure SGX's survival and also to ensure it remains competitive.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Its ability to attract listings and provide liquidity for companies will, eventually, translate, in part, into SGX's profits and eventual contributions to FSDF annually and feed into the pool of funds already accumulated in the FSDF.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: SGX is and remains an important financial vehicle for companies to raise capital through listing on the exchange.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In doing so, it also offers opportunities for many retail investors, especially retirees who have some knowledge of the mechanics of stock trading, to try to add value to their savings.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Companies use it to raise operating capital, while the investors use it with the hope to earn regular dividends and, hopefully, a rise in investment value.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Certainly, for SGX, the competition is great, for it has to contend with the regional markets, especially Hong Kong, as well as markets in Europe and particularly, in the US.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But can the Minister share MAS' vision of how an exchange, such as SGX, can play a pivotal role in enhancing financial sector development and financial innovations, to drive Singapore’s long-term economic growth, especially given the challenges exchanges globally are facing currently, not only from direct competition, from regional exchanges, but also from technological disruption and various other ways of capital raising externally.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The current EDMA does not allow SEL, a special purpose company, to hold SGX shares for the benefit of Financial Sector Development Fund (FSDF), to elect to receive new SGX shares.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This move to amend the EDMA will provide SEL with the flexibility to participate in SGX's corporate actions in a cost-effective manner and accord it the means to exercise rights similar to other shareholders of SGX.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This legislative move is crucial to ensure that the core principles of EDMA and SEL are maintained, whilst allowing SEL, SGX's strategic investor, to support the exchange in strengthening its working capital position, with the option to retain cash with SDS.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It is in this spirit that I would like to seek the Minister of State's response on three areas of inquiry which, I believe, will better clarify the Bill’s impact.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Since its inception, FSDF allows MAS to support financial sector transformation and has provided strategic funding to support the development of Singapore as a global financial hub.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It is critical that FSDF’s wide-ranging development initiatives, from skills upgrading, R&D to infrastructure development, must not be constrained in any way.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For instance, FSDF launched a $125 million support package in April 2020 to augment the growth of Singapore’s fintech sectors and accelerate digitalisation.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: In the same year, FSDF also enhanced the Financial Sector Technology and Innovation Scheme to boost our talent pipelines for Singaporeans into fintech.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I applaud the meritorious development projects that FSDF has been supporting over the years and urge MAS to continue investing strongly in the development of the Singapore financial sector.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: However, given that we are not quite yet out of the woods as far as the pandemic is concerned, I would like to ask the Minister about the impact to SGX's cash dividend funding for FSDF initiatives with SDS.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Apart from SGX dividends, what other sources of income does FSDF receive?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: How dependent is FSDF on SGX dividends, in order to maintain its portfolio of projects, both in the medium and long term?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: My second inquiry focuses on the Bill's impact on SEL's influence on SGX.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: With the SDS, dominant shareholders, such as SEL, are in a position to potentially increase their stake over time should they elect to receive SGX shares whilst other investors may choose otherwise.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It is worth noting that for MAS to play a dual role as SGX's regulator and FSDF's administrator without conflict of interest, safeguards were in place at the time of EDMA's introduction.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, SGX shares held by SEL are non-voting.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Despite such safeguards, the action of a dominant shareholder with non-voting interest can still indirectly influence shares performance by virtue of options in its dividend policy.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Efficient corporate governance can be achieved with the use of non-voting shares, provided that robust governance delineating voting and non-voting shares is in place to motivate actors to align with intended goals.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: As at present, SGX shares held by SEL are still ambiguously classed despite the non-voting clause.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For instance, these shares are still classed as ordinary shares that possess the possibility to be used for controlling interest purposes when sold to other investors upon approval by the Minister-in-charge.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The introduction of scrip dividend further increases SEL's ability to amass a higher proportion of these ambiguously classed SGX shares.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What are the considerations to vary or maintain the shareholding of SGX shares under SEL with SDS?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Furthermore, SEL's decision to elect scrip or cash dividend may invite unnecessary speculation, due to the perceived information asymmetry between dominant and minority shareholders.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: How will this issue be managed going forward?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Speaker, Sir, it is also rather counter-intuitive for a significant and strategic investor, such as SEL, to hold non-voting shares.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: How will the future of SGX be safeguarded if voting rights to direct the company do not rest with the largest and strategic investor?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: How will we safeguard the situation to prevent a group of SGX shareholders from forming a large enough segment of voting power and choose to exercise it in situations where they will move SGX in the wrong direction.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: More broadly, this Bill also comes at a time when SGX has recently announced the introduction of Special Purpose Acquisition Companies (SPACs) into the bourse.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Market watchers expect SPACs to boost SGX’s position as a key financial hub in Asia, with SGX gaining from an overall higher valuation with the listing of tech-related and new economy companies.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: However, SPACs have also received mixed market reactions from institutional and retail investors alike, including the potential downsides and risks of SPACs to retail investors.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: What is the impact to SGX from an overall valuation of the Singapore market with the entry of SPACs?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: More specifically, would this have any bearings on SEL’s stake in SGX in the future?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Notwithstanding the points above, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Ms He Ting Ru and Ms Foo Mee Har had asked about safeguards over potential conflicts of interests when MAS both regulates SGX and also administers the FSDF.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Ms Foo Mee Har had also asked whether more could be done to clarify the nature of SEL's holdings and if SEL could, inadvertently, influence the outcome of a scrip dividend exercise by signalling its intent.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS does not derive any income or loss from SGX shares.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Dividends from SGX shares are channelled to FSDF for the benefit of the financial sector as a whole.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Bill has provided that this same safeguard on non-voting rights will also apply to new shares received.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The non-voting nature of SEL’s shareholdings is disclosed in SGX’s financial statements.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In addition, SEL has independent directors who owe a fiduciary duty to SEL.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The directors are nominated by MOM, MTI and both public agencies have economic and manpower development mandates that are similar to the objectives of FSDF.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Next, regarding any SGX scrip dividend scheme, all shareholders would make their own assessments, taking into account their individual circumstances in deciding whether to elect for new shares in a scrip dividend scheme or not.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Shareholders' decisions are, typically, not announced while the election period is ongoing.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about the governance structure of FSDF and how MAS ensures that FSDF’s expenditures are aligned with FSDF's objectives.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS takes a rolling five-year view for planning of FSDF's grant expenditure.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is in view of the relatively long gestation period of most development initiatives, such as developing industry-wide infrastructure, developing local talent in emerging finance areas and promoting financial innovation and technologies.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The Minister-in-charge of MAS approves the strategic allocation of FSDF's monies on a rolling five-year basis and based on that approved allocation, the Managing Director of MAS approves FSDF's annual budgets and MAS publishes FSDF's financial statements annually.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Grant schemes are developed and, periodically, also reviewed to ensure that the funding provided does, indeed, meet industry’s needs.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In recent years, there has been an increase in FSDF's funding to support skills upgrading and reskilling initiatives and financial institutions' push to adopt financial technology and innovation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Individual projects seeking FSDF's funding are also subject to robust governance and controls.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: To ensure the prudent usage of FSDF's funds, the fund is administered in compliance with MOF's guidance on grants governance, notwithstanding that FSDF is not funded by taxpayers' monies, given that it was set up using the proceeds from the demutualisation of privately-owned exchanges, which I described earlier.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Taken together, these measures help to ensure that FSDF's expenditure is aligned with FSDF's objectives and that the funds are used prudently.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat also asked about recent trends of FSDF's expenditure, how the pandemic has affected FSDF's expenditure and the take-up of specific FSDF-funded schemes, while Ms He Ting Ru also sought an update on the role of FSDF.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: FSDF currently supports a wide range of initiatives across talent development, technology and innovation.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It also supports other initiatives on financial sector activities and consumer education.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Pre-COVID-19, FSDF's annual expenditures were within $90 million.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This includes the $125 million package that was launched in April 2020 alluded to by Mr Saktiandi Supaat.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As part of the support package, MAS increased course fee subsidies for relevant IBF courses and extended the subsidies to include local employees of fintech firms.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As a result, we have seen a very strong response from financial institutions in tapping on the funding available to upskill and reskill their financial professionals.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Training participation has increased significantly since the launch of enhanced support in April 2020.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: The FSDF also supports efforts in developing multiple pathways to build our pipeline of local financial sector talent.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This has resulted in financial institutions committing in 2020 and 2021 to hire and to train close to 1,100 Singaporeans as part of their structured management associate programmes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In addition, the FSDF has also supported over 280 outstanding Singaporeans to acquire specialist skills through postgraduate studies in areas, such as data science, financial engineering and risk management.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As for the Cybersecurity Capability Grant (CCG) scheme, it aims to develop local cybersecurity talent in our financial services sector.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: By supporting financial institutions to set up or expand regional and specialised cybersecurity teams in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Since 2019, five financial institutions have tapped on this CCG to anchor their regional cybersecurity capabilities here in Singapore, generating 60 new cybersecurity positions here.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: To Mr Saktiandi Supaat’s question on FSDF's support for nascent areas, such as blockchain technology and carbon credits, FSDF has, indeed, supported such projects where they have the potential to strengthen our competitive advantage as a financial centre.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Given that FSDF provides funding for a wide range of initiatives that support the development of Singapore as a global financial hub, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Ms Foo Mee Har have asked whether giving SEL the option to elect for scrip dividends, in lieu of cash, could constrain FSDF’s ability in supporting the financial sector going forward.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Ms He Ting Ru has also asked how SEL would fund its participation in SGX subscription offers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Similarly, the decision for SEL to participate in subscription offers and how SEL funds its participation in any subscription offers, will also have to be approved by the Minister-in-charge of MAS.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: FSDF has tripled in size since its inception in 1999.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This is so because MAS has been prudent in managing FSDF's total grant expenditure and especially because of the compounding effect of the returns on its investment of FSDF funds over the years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Next, Members were interested to understand how, in the absence of voting rights, FSDF is kept assured that the value of its holdings in SGX is upheld.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In a related vein, Ms He and Mr Saktiandi had also asked about how SGX plans to keep up with competition and technological disruptions, given that the FSDF is partly funded by SGX's dividends and shares.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: As I just mentioned, FSDF's fund size has tripled since its inception in 1999.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will continue to be disciplined in managing FSDF's grants and investing the surpluses in a diversified investment portfolio, so as to sustain FSDF's ability to support financial sector development initiatives over the long term.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On SGX's efforts to build and retain competitiveness, an area of interest by all of Members who have spoken on this Bill, please allow me to reply briefly at this point.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: SGX has made progress in its strategy to build a multi-asset exchange.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In addition to the equities market that Mr Saktiandi had mentioned, SGX is a key bond listing venue in Asia and offers a strong suite of derivatives for risk hedging across a wide range of asset classes.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, you have equities, you have bonds, you have derivatives.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: In recent years, SGX has been building up its bond trading and FX capabilities and pursued initiatives to enhance connectivity, including the latest collaboration on an ETF Product Link with Shenzhen Stock Exchange.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: But as Ms He and other Members mentioned earlier, SGX faces keen competition, not just regionally but also internationally from many different exchanges across the world.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: So, it will have to continually evolve its strategies, evolve all its offerings in response to the emerging competition, so that it is not standing still.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: They could include innovation, digitalisation efforts to streamline their processes and enhance efficiencies for the industry, harnessing new trends such as the growth in sustainable investing and building synergistic links with other exchanges.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: Ms He also asked for MAS' position on allowing SGX shareholders to increase their stakes to be above 5%.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: This will also provide FSDF with an additional option to generate income for the fund.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: And this is important because the fund, FSDF, as I have mentioned, is to drive growth and create good jobs for Singaporeans in a very dynamic and fast-evolving financial sector in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.
